skill.name: youtube-thumbnail-design
skill.description: Design YouTube thumbnails with practical rules for size, contrast, safe zones, text, facial expressions, and mobile readability.
skill.summary: Create readable, high-contrast YouTube thumbnails that work at mobile feed size.

content.value_statement: YouTube thumbnails must be clear at mobile feed size and still earn clicks. This skill gives practical rules for layout, color, text, faces, and A/B testing.
actual_capabilities: Defines YouTube thumbnail dimensions, aspect ratio, file size, and supported formats.
Explains how to test thumbnail readability at 120 pixels wide.
Identifies safe zones around timestamps, chapter markers, progress bars, and crop edges.
Gives contrast, color count, font size, and text length rules for readable thumbnails.
Maps facial expressions and composition choices to common video goals.
Provides belt CLI prompt examples for tutorial, review, listicle, and A/B test thumbnails.
limitations: Image generation examples require the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
The skill does not upload thumbnails or read YouTube Studio analytics.
CTR guidance is heuristic and should be tested against each channel audience.
Generated images may need brand, likeness, and rights review before publishing.

use_cases.title: Plan a Creator Thumbnail
use_cases.description: Choose a readable composition, strong color pair, and short text for a new YouTube upload.

use_cases.title: Create Video Series Templates
use_cases.description: Build repeatable thumbnail patterns that keep a channel recognizable without making every image look identical.

use_cases.title: Run Thumbnail Experiments
use_cases.description: Define controlled A/B thumbnail variants that test one visual variable at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Thumbnail Idea
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before design work starts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this YouTube video idea and suggest one thumbnail concept that passes the 120px mobile readability test: [video idea].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Safe Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a thumbnail layout plan for this video: [title]. Include safe zones, focal point, text placement, and a three-color palette.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Image Prompt Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Write three AI image prompts for a YouTube thumbnail about [topic]. Vary expression, background, and composition while keeping text readable.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an A/B Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create two thumbnail variants for [video topic]. Keep one variable different, explain the hypothesis, and list what to measure after publishing.

output_examples.input: A tutorial video titled “Build a Portfolio Website in One Hour.”
output: Use a clean workspace with a laptop as the main subject.
Place the creator face on the left and the result preview on the right.
Use blue and orange contrast with no more than four words of text.

output_examples.input: A product comparison video for two microphones.
output: Show both products facing each other with a clear versus marker.
Use one bright accent color for each side of the comparison.
Avoid placing logos or key details near the bottom-right timestamp area.

output_examples.input: A request to improve a cluttered thumbnail concept.
output: Reduce the concept to one focal subject, one emotion, and one short text phrase.
Increase contrast between the subject and background.
Preview the design at 120 pixels wide before creating final variants.

best_practices: Test every concept at 120 pixels wide before treating it as finished.
Use one clear focal point and reserve corners for platform overlays.
Change only one major visual variable when comparing A/B variants.
anti_patterns: Do not add text that repeats the full video title.
Do not place important faces, logos, or results under YouTube overlay areas.
Do not rely on tiny details that disappear in the mobile feed.

faq.question: Does this skill generate thumbnails directly?
faq.answer: It includes belt CLI examples for AI image generation, but users need the inference.sh CLI and account access.

faq.question: What thumbnail size does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends at least 1280 by 720 pixels, with 1920 by 1080 pixels preferred.

faq.question: Can it improve click-through rate?
faq.answer: It provides CTR-focused design rules, but results depend on audience, topic, title, and testing.

faq.question: Does it cover mobile readability?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes checking thumbnails at about 120 pixels wide, where many viewers first see them.

faq.question: Does it support A/B testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to create variants by changing one variable at a time.

faq.question: Is this only for creators who show their face?
faq.answer: No. It covers face-based thumbnails and faceless patterns such as tutorials, comparisons, and listicles.
